scope.grouping: same company attempt, exact successful final URL including query, at least two distinct saved requested URLs
scope.successful_body: primary snapshot only; http_get_attempted true; actual start within completed batch interval; HTTP2xx; nonempty decoded text; no error
scope.event_identity: http_get_started_at + actual response URL (or attempted URL if response absent); cached robots metadata deduplicated across all company sources in a batch
scope.event_start_time: offset-aware http_get_started_at; legacy retrieved_at and HTTP Date are not dispatch timestamps

hash_definitions.snapshot_file_sha256: SHA256 of the existing saved JSON bytes, frozen at read time
hash_definitions.response_body_sha256: existing source.sha256 of response content bytes before charset decoding; requests iter_content may already decompress transfer content
hash_definitions.extracted_visible_text_sha256: derived SHA256 of saved source.text encoded as UTF-8

scope.record_ref_policy: matching attempted_at and completed_at within the collection run; referenced archives preferred; latest_attempt child may be used; selected time/fetch fields frozen here
scope.legacy_current_record_refs_mutable: record source SHA is the read-time version; frozen attempt fields and immutable primary snapshot hashes remain available if future record review changes the file

conclusion: Repeated final-body GETs are a small observed fraction; this sample does not support duplicate retrieval as the principal source of load. No collector change is proposed.
limitations: A same final URL alone does not imply equal content; body SHA and visible-text differences are recorded.
The eight final re-fetches are an observed lower bound, not a guarantee that all later alias redirect requests can be removed safely.
Raw body bytes are not stored, so byte-level causes of differing response SHA cannot be reconstructed.
Cross-query final URLs remain distinct; query-stripped grouping is diagnostic only.

Reported run GET counts are authoritative totals. Intermediate-origin robots may be absent from returned capture metadata after a cross-origin body redirect, so saved-node event reconstruction can have a residual.
These are three completed batches with no common transport503; they do not establish behavior for the whole universe or an outage cause.
